title: A Qualified AANEC Trapped-Surface Bound for Non-Black-Hole Stellar Remnants
abstract: This idea refines the proposed AANEC-based theorem that a bound on the maximum mass of a non-black-hole compact remnant could be derived and that the observed 2-5 solar-mass gap would follow from horizon-formation necessity. The limitation being repaired is that averaged null energy conditions are weaker than the pointwise null/strong energy conditions used in Penrose-type trapped-surface arguments, and the observed stellar mass gap is strongly affected by supernova explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, and binary evolution. We therefore construct a qualified formal theorem or conjecture: in classical general relativity under spherical symmetry, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, AANEC, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, a compactness threshold forces trapped-surface formation and bounds the maximum mass of stable horizonless compact remnants within the stated model class. The 2-5 solar-mass gap is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint, not a direct numerical consequence of the theorem.
method: The method repairs the original AANEC mass-gap proposal by replacing an unqualified derivation of the 2-5 solar-mass gap with a bounded theorem/conjecture. Starting from Penrose-type trapped-surface arguments, it substitutes pointwise NEC/SEC assumptions with AANEC along complete null generators, then adds an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition sufficient for Raychaudhuri-type focusing. Using spherical collapse geometry and Misner-Sharp compactness, it derives a threshold compactness or mass scale above which a stable horizonless remnant cannot avoid trapped-surface formation within the model class. TOV-like stellar-structure assumptions are used to translate the compactness threshold into an upper mass bound for non-black-hole remnants. Boundary tests include AANEC violation, failure of averaged focusing, incomplete null generators, quantum stress-energy corrections, rotation, anisotropy, and nonspherical collapse. The observed 2-5 solar-mass gap is then compared only as an astrophysical consistency check, not as a theorem-derived prediction.
introduction: Black holes arise when stellar remnants collapse beyond a critical compactness, but formalizing this threshold under realistic matter assumptions remains challenging. Classical Penrose-type trapped-surface arguments rely on pointwise energy conditions, yet many physically relevant fields violate them. Building on the insights of “Energy conditions in general relativity and quantum field theory,” averaged null energy conditions (AANEC) offer a more robust route to focusing theorems, though they are weaker than pointwise NEC/SEC assumptions and may not by themselves force trapped-surface formation. The mature idea anchor proposed deriving the observed 2–5 M☉ lower mass gap directly from AANEC-based horizon necessity. This paper refines that proposal by repairing its key limitation: the gap is strongly affected by supernova explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, and binary evolution, as emphasized in the remaining survey-cited papers. We therefore construct a qualified formal theorem or conjecture: in classical general relativity under spherical symmetry, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, AANEC, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, a compactness threshold forces trapped-surface formation and bounds the maximum mass of stable horizonless compact remnants within the stated model class. The 2–5 M☉ gap is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint, not a direct numerical consequence of the theorem. Boundary tests examine AANEC violation, failure of averaged focusing, incomplete null generators, quantum stress-energy corrections, rotation, anisotropy, and nonspherical collapse.

Relax pointwise NEC/SEC to AANEC along complete null generators and add an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition as an independent geometric assumption.
Construct the target relation: define Misner-Sharp compactness C=2GM/(Rc^2) and a threshold C_* above which Raychaudhuri-type focusing forces a trapped surface.
Derive the horizon-formation implication: show that any stable horizonless remnant in the model class must satisfy C<C_*, and exceeding C_* yields trapped-surface/black-hole formation.
Bound the compact_remnant_mass_bound by translating C_* into a maximum mass M_max_nonBH using TOV-like stellar-structure assumptions for radius, pressure, and equation-of-state regularity.

Verify the proof by checking the pointwise_energy_boundary: compare the AANEC-plus-averaged-focusing theorem with classical pointwise NEC/SEC trapped-surface arguments and identify where the relaxation is genuine or where the added focusing assumption is as restrictive.

Construct counterexample_boundary cases: AANEC violation, insufficient averaged focusing, incomplete null generators, quantum stress-energy corrections, rotation, anisotropy, nonspherical collapse, or exotic horizonless objects that evade the assumptions.

Compare lower_mass_gap_relation only as an astrophysical consistency check: if M_max_nonBH overlaps the observed 2-5 solar-mass gap, report consistency; if not, attribute discrepancy to stellar-evolution, explosion, fallback, equation-of-state, binary, or selection effects rather than theorem failure.

directions.title: AANEC-Relaxed Trapped Surface Theorem and Stellar Mass-Gap Derivation
directions.abstract: This direction replaces pointwise null/strong energy assumptions in Penrose-type trapped-surface arguments with an averaged null energy condition (AANEC), but only as part of a qualified theorem construction. Under classical GR, spherical symmetry, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition along relevant null generators, the AANEC-based argument is intended to yield a trapped-surface threshold and an upper compactness/mass scale for stable non-black-hole remnants within the stated model class. The observed 2-5 solar mass gap is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint, not a purely theorem-derived consequence, because explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, and binary evolution can independently shape the remnant mass distribution.

hypothesis.central_hypothesis: If spherically symmetric stellar collapse satisfies AANEC, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, then reaching a model-dependent compactness threshold forces trapped-surface formation; consequently, stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale are excluded within this restricted model class. This does not by itself explain the observed 2-5 solar mass gap, which may be governed by supernova explosion physics, fallback, equation-of-state uncertainties, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, or binary interactions.

The observed mass gap is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint, with alternative stellar-physics mechanisms identified as confounders.

debate_trace.target_claim: AANEC on collapsing null generators of a trapped or marginally outer trapped tube yields a state-independent mass-gap/compactness horizon bound for supermassive stellar collapse, such that microphysical equation-of-state details cannot remove the bound within the stated validity domain.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate overstates AANEC as a state-independent physical condition and treats the mass-gap bound as established. AANEC is an assumption on stress-energy, not a theorem for all classical matter, and the postulated mass-gap bound requires an additional trapped/MOTT-tube and quasi-local mass/area relation; it does not by itself prove black-hole formation or initial trapped-surface formation.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: Black-hole formation in realistic stellar collapse can remain equation-of-state dependent because the formation of a trapped surface, bounce behavior, and semiclassical negative-energy effects are not controlled by AANEC alone; a different EoS may avoid the assumed trapped tube or violate the averaged null-energy integral even if macroscopic collapse data are similar.
debate_trace.required_revision: Reduce the claim to a conditional compactness/trapped-surface bound under explicit AANEC, trapped/MOTT-tube formation, asymptotic flatness, and a specified quasi-local mass/area relation; remove the implication that AANEC alone proves a universal mass gap or black-hole existence.
alternative_explanations: Equation-of-state details can control whether a trapped or marginally outer trapped tube forms before horizon formation.
Bounce or semiclassical negative-energy effects can evade AANEC-based focusing without contradicting macroscopic stellar-collapse data.
The observed black-hole mass distribution may reflect astrophysical formation channels rather than a universal AANEC-derived mass gap.
debate_trace.final_scope: Classical four-dimensional asymptotically flat supermassive stellar collapse, conditional on a trapped or marginally outer trapped tube and AANEC along its collapsing null generators, with a specified quasi-local mass/area relation; the result is a state-independence bound among AANEC-satisfying EoS families, not a universal black-hole existence proof or unconditional mass gap.

alternative_explanations: Event-horizon formation can be defined globally and may occur in some models without a closed trapped surface, so trapped-surface criteria are sufficient certificates rather than necessary conditions.
Complete burnout can fail to produce a black hole if the remnant is subcritical, bounces, or violates the null energy condition, but those cases lie outside the classical theorem's validity domain.

Penrose's theorem yields future null geodesic incompleteness; identifying a black-hole region additionally requires asymptotic predictability, weak cosmic censorship, or an equivalent hiding assumption.
debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified formal sufficiency theorem: in smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic spacetimes with NEC-respecting matter and a hiding assumption (asymptotic predictability or weak cosmic censorship), closed trapped-surface formation is sufficient to certify black-hole existence via a nonempty event horizon and future null geodesic incompleteness; it is not claimed necessary, and NEC-violating, bouncing, non-asymptotically-flat, or naked-singularity scenarios are excluded.

debate_trace.target_claim: In smooth, spherically symmetric, NEC-respecting, asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic stellar collapse with a hiding assumption (asymptotic predictability or weak cosmic censorship), the existence of a closed trapped surface is sufficient to certify black-hole existence via a nonempty event horizon and future null geodesic incompleteness; it is not asserted to be necessary.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The original formulation can be read as conflating Penrose singularity incompleteness with event-horizon existence and does not exclude transient or non-outer trapped surfaces as alternative explanations for the same geometric observation.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: A competing mechanism or confounder could explain the same observation: a hidden-singularity assumption, a transient trapped surface, NEC-violating bounce, mass loss, or non-asymptotically flat cosmological setting could produce or block the inferred black-hole existence relation.
debate_trace.required_revision: Narrow the certificate to a future outer trapped surface or persistent trapped tube, keep the hiding condition as an explicit separate assumption, and add countermodel boundaries for transient trapped surfaces and naked-singularity alternatives.
alternative_explanations: A closed trapped surface may be transient or not future outer trapped, so it need not certify a persistent black-hole region.
Future null geodesic incompleteness may be a singularity result without event-horizon existence unless a hiding or censorship condition is assumed.
Complete burnout, bounce, pressure reversal, or NEC-violating effects could mimic or block the inferred collapse route.
Non-asymptotically flat or cosmological settings can produce trapped surfaces without asymptotic-flatness event horizons.
debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified conditional classical GR sufficiency claim: future outer trapped-surface formation, or in spherical symmetry a persistent trapped tube, certifies a nonempty event-horizon black-hole region and future null geodesic incompleteness only under explicit hiding, NEC, asymptotic flatness, global hyperbolicity, and no-bounce assumptions; no necessity claim and no extension to NEC-violating, non-spherical, cosmological, naked-singularity, or quantum-gravity regimes.

debate_trace.target_claim: In stellar_collapse_validity, the existence of a closed future-trapped surface S together with trapped_surface_conditional_focusing_bound along every future null generator of J^+(S) entails null geodesic incompleteness and event_horizon_formation, even when the global pointwise null_energy_condition fails.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate conflates Penrose-type incompleteness with event-horizon formation, uses 'generators of J^+(S)' too broadly, and defines the integrated focusing bound too vaguely: a merely nonnegative cumulative integral is not automatically a sufficient Raychaudhuri comparison condition unless it is specified along the null congruence orthogonal to S, with partial-integral or weighted bounds and an affine-parameter threshold.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: Assuming a closed future-trapped surface may already presuppose the black-hole causal structure, making the premise inversion circular, and the relaxed bound may collapse to the null energy condition in ordinary collapse where shear is negligible or where no explicit non-equivalence countermodel is supplied.
debate_trace.required_revision: Narrow the claim to a relaxed Penrose focusing theorem for future null geodesics orthogonal to S; define the bound as a sufficient partial-integrated Ricci-plus-shear comparison condition; separate event-horizon existence as a conditional consequence of the trapped-surface-to-horizon theorem under asymptotic flatness and global hyperbolicity; and require an explicit countermodel showing non-equivalence with pointwise null_energy_condition.
alternative_explanations: The original pointwise null_energy_condition may already be sufficient for Penrose-type incompleteness, so the integrated relaxation adds value only if a genuine non-equivalence countermodel exists.
Event-horizon existence may follow directly from trapped-surface plus asymptotic-flatness/global-hyperbolicity assumptions, independent of the relaxed focusing bound.
Gravitational-wave population inference may provide statistical proxies for black-hole formation but cannot by itself identify trapped-surface formation as the mechanism.
debate_trace.final_scope: A qualified formal theorem-or-condition-relaxation in classical stellar-collapse validity: the integrated bound is a relaxed sufficient condition for Penrose-type null incompleteness along trapped-surface generators, while event-horizon/black-hole-region existence is conditional on the standard trapped-surface-to-horizon implication and is not inferred from merger statistics.

debate_trace.target_claim: A closed future-trapped surface plus a local integrated Ricci-plus-shear focusing bound along its orthogonal null generators is a relaxed sufficient premise for Penrose-type black-hole existence, with event-horizon existence following from a trapped-surface-to-horizon causal theorem in classical stellar-collapse spacetimes.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate must separate the integrated focusing result, which yields conjugate points and null geodesic incompleteness, from the stronger global event-horizon conclusion, which requires an additional trapped-surface-to-horizon causal implication and should not be treated as automatic.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: A competing formal mechanism or confounder could explain the same black-hole conclusion: pointwise NEC, averaged integral energy conditions, apparent-horizon formation, or low-shear collapse may make the proposed integrated bound non-distinct, while gravitational-wave population statistics could be explained by astrophysical proxies without establishing this local causal mechanism.
debate_trace.required_revision: Reduce the claim scope by making the event-horizon conclusion conditional on a separately proven trapped-surface-to-horizon implication, specify the integrated bound as a comparison-time sufficient condition, and require a countermodel demonstrating genuine relaxation rather than equivalence to pointwise NEC.
alternative_explanations: Pointwise null energy condition, averaged null energy conditions, or other integral focusing assumptions could produce the same Penrose incompleteness result, so the proposed bound may not be a unique formal mechanism.
Apparent-horizon or marginally-trapped-tube formation, or numerical-relativity criteria, could explain black-hole formation without invoking the proposed event-horizon causal implication.

Gravitational-wave population statistics, electromagnetic observations, or stellar-evolution channels could be explained by astrophysical formation pathways and proxies without establishing the local trapped-surface mechanism.
Low-shear collapse may make the integrated Ricci-plus-shear bound effectively equivalent to pointwise NEC, weakening the claimed premise relaxation.
debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified formal condition-relaxation in classical, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat stellar-collapse spacetimes: a comparison-time integrated Ricci-plus-shear focusing bound along orthogonal null generators of a smooth closed future-trapped surface is a sufficient condition for conjugate points and null geodesic incompleteness; black-hole-region or event-horizon existence is asserted only conditionally if a separate trapped-surface-to-horizon causal theorem holds. The claim does not explain why trapped surfaces form and does not infer black-hole existence from gravitational-wave population statistics.

debate_trace.target_claim: For future-complete, asymptotically flat, classical-GR non-black-hole compact remnants with a regular surface and positive compactness boundary C_min, compact-support AANEC focusing yields a maximum non-black-hole mass remnant_mass_bound; exceeding this bound destroys compact_object_validity_domain and forces trapped-surface formation, and mapping the bound over admissible stellar remnant radii derives the observed 2-5 solar-mass lower mass gap.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The claim overstates the formal result: AANEC/null convergence plus C_min > 0 does not by itself give a universal remnant_mass_bound or derive the observed 2-5 solar-mass gap; an explicit radius-mass admissibility domain, a proof that integrated null convergence forces a trapped surface, and a cosmic-censorship/global assumption for horizon language are missing. AANEC is also a semiclassical/expectation-value condition, so calling the setting purely classical GR is imprecise.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: The lower mass gap may be explained by stellar-evolution fallback, pair-instability supernovae, uncertain nuclear equation-of-state physics, or observational selection, and horizonless ultracompact objects may evade the proposed bound by violating regularity, energy conditions, future completeness, asymptotic flatness, or the assumed radius-mass domain.
debate_trace.required_revision: Reduce the claim to a conditional AANEC/null-convergence compactness-radius theorem with an explicit radius-mass domain and a trapped-surface rather than unconditional horizon conclusion; replace direct derivation of the observed 2-5 solar-mass gap with a possible mapping that requires stellar-structure/causality constraints.
alternative_explanations: stellar-evolution fallback and explosion energetics
pair-instability and pulsational pair-instability supernova physics
uncertain nuclear equation of state and remnant radius-mass relations
observational selection and detection biases in the reported lower mass gap
horizonless ultracompact objects evading the bound through exotic matter or boundary conditions
quantum-gravity or semiclassical corrections violating compact-support AANEC
debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified conditional formal-theoretical scope: AANEC/null-convergence plus compactness-radius boundary theorem for future-complete asymptotically flat regular non-black-hole remnants in effective classical GR with expectation-value stress energy; it may yield a forbidden mass interval and a candidate boundary interpretation of the stellar lower mass gap only after mapping an admissible radius-mass domain, and it is not a universal proof of black-hole existence or a direct derivation of the observed 2-5 solar-mass gap.

debate_trace.target_claim: For future-complete, asymptotically flat, regular non-black-hole remnants satisfying compact-support AANEC/integrated null convergence up to controlled semiclassical offset, a positive compactness boundary C_min, and an explicit admissible radius-mass domain, masses above M_bound cannot remain trapped-surface-free; if M_bound maps to the reported stellar lower-mass interval, the gap may have a formal boundary interpretation.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The theorem's connection to the observed 2-5 solar-mass lower mass gap is conditional on a radius-mass mapping and does not by itself establish a causal astrophysical explanation.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: The same interval could be produced by supernova fallback, pair-instability mass loss, equation-of-state uncertainty, binary interactions, or selection effects without invoking a trapped-surface theorem boundary.
debate_trace.required_revision: Separate the formal trapped-surface theorem from the mass-gap interpretation: state that the lower-mass-gap mapping is a candidate consequence only if M_bound lies in that interval, and that competing astrophysical mechanisms remain viable unless a formal counterexample boundary plus explicit radius-mass mapping rules them out.
alternative_explanations: supernova fallback and natal kick distributions
pair-instability and pulsational pair-instability mass loss
uncertain stellar equation of state and remnant radius-mass relation
binary interaction, common-envelope evolution, and accretion history
selection effects, detection thresholds, and population-synthesis uncertainties
debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified formal-theoretical scope: a conditional upper-mass/trapped-surface theorem for specified regular non-black-hole remnants under compact-support AANEC, positive compactness boundary, and an explicit admissible radius-mass domain; the stellar lower-mass-gap interpretation is only a possible mapping consequence and not a causal explanation of observed populations.

debate_trace.target_claim: In gravitational collapse satisfying aanec_state_independent_inequality, future-trapped-surface existence, and mass_gap_horizon_bound hypotheses, horizon formation requires the minimum compactness or mass condition derived in horizon_formation_bound_derivation, and this condition is state-independent because it is carried by aanec_state_independent_horizon_lemma rather than by microphysical_eos_independence.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate overstates the formal reach of AANEC and a mass-gap horizon bound. AANEC supplies integrated null-energy focusing, but it does not by itself yield a universal minimum mass or a horizon-formation mass gap in classical GR, where scale invariance and the absence of a general mass-gap theorem prevent such a conclusion. The claim becomes scientifically consistent only if mass_gap_horizon_bound is reinterpreted as an explicit geometric mass-area or compactness hypothesis, and if future-trapped-surface existence, complete horizon generators, and cosmic-censorship/event-horizon identification are stated as separate assumptions.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: The strongest objection is circularity or hidden dependence: the mass_gap_horizon_bound may secretly encode stellar-structure, equation-of-state, or quantum-gravity assumptions, while AANEC may fail in semiclassical regimes. If so, the lemma does not replace microphysical EoS independence with a genuinely state-independent causal-geometric condition.
debate_trace.required_revision: Recast the candidate as a conditional formal theorem: define mass_gap_horizon_bound as an explicit geometric mass-area/compactness hypothesis rather than a universal minimum mass, add complete-null-generator and cosmic-censorship/event-horizon assumptions, restrict state independence to the absence of explicit microphysical EoS in the hypotheses, and make the proof obligation the derivation of a conditional horizon-formation bound from AANEC plus the geometric mass-gap/compactness hypothesis.
alternative_explanations: Black-hole formation may be better grounded in Penrose-type trapped-surface theorems using NEC, global hyperbolicity, and cosmic censorship rather than AANEC plus a mass-gap bound.
Equation-of-state-specific stellar instability or pressure-supported collapse may be the operative mechanism in particular astrophysical pathways.
The hoop conjecture or numerical collapse criteria may explain horizon formation through geometric concentration of energy rather than a universal mass gap.
A true minimum mass could arise only from quantum-gravity or Planck-scale assumptions, not from classical GR alone.
Semiclassical violations of AANEC could invalidate the proposed state-independent energy-condition carrier.
debate_trace.final_scope: The claim is acceptable only as a conditional formal theorem: under asymptotically flat classical or controlled semiclassical collapse, future-trapped-surface existence, complete horizon generators, AANEC or a bounded relaxation, cosmic censorship, and an explicitly geometric mass-area/compactness hypothesis, one may derive a lower bound on a geometric compactness or mass parameter sufficient for horizon formation. State independence means no explicit microphysical EoS appears in the hypotheses, not that a universal minimum mass is proven.

debate_trace.target_claim: AANEC along complete null generators plus trapped-surface geometry plus an explicit geometric mass-gap/compactness hypothesis entails a conditional lower bound on geometric compactness or mass parameter sufficient for horizon formation.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate risks being read as a state-independent explanation of black-hole formation, whereas it is only a conditional sufficient bound and may be redundant with Penrose-type trapped-surface or other geometric criteria.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: Horizon formation could follow from Penrose trapped-surface theorems, apparent-horizon dynamics, hoop-conjecture-like conditions, or numerical collapse without the proposed AANEC/mass-gap lemma.
debate_trace.required_revision: Reduce the claim to a non-exclusive sufficient theorem and explicitly distinguish Penrose-type trapped-surface, apparent-horizon, hoop-conjecture-like, and numerical-collapse alternatives.
alternative_explanations: Penrose trapped-surface theorems may imply black-hole formation or singularity formation under weaker or different causal-geometric assumptions.
Apparent-horizon formation in numerical collapse may provide a dynamical explanation independent of the proposed mass-gap/AANEC lemma.
Hoop-conjecture-like geometric compactness conditions may serve as alternative sufficient criteria for horizon formation.
Equation-of-state-specific stellar collapse, rotation, pressure support, or asymmetric dynamical effects may explain horizon formation without invoking a state-independent AANEC bound.
debate_trace.final_scope: A conditional, non-exclusive sufficient theorem for horizon formation under AANEC, trapped-surface, completeness, cosmic-censorship/event-horizon, and geometric mass-area/compactness assumptions; not a necessary, observational, or unique explanation of black-hole existence.

debate_trace.target_claim: In classical asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic general relativity, a closed future outer trapped surface arising from supermassive stellar collapse initial data, together with a bounded averaged null energy condition relaxation, entails future null-geodesic incompleteness and black-hole region formation; removing the trapped surface or violating the bounded energy condition blocks the implication.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate overstates Penrose's theorem by treating a trapped surface plus an unspecified bounded ANEC relaxation as sufficient for event-horizon formation, and it allows compactness C = 2GM/(Rc^2) > 1 to stand in for a rigorous trapped-surface condition; the ANEC relaxation also needs a quantitative focusing bound.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: A spacetime could satisfy high compactness or a weak energy-condition relaxation yet fail to form a closed trapped surface, form a naked singularity, or lack a well-defined event horizon; direct observational evidence remains outside the formal theorem.
debate_trace.required_revision: Narrow the conclusion to future null-geodesic incompleteness and a nonempty black-hole region under explicit trapped-surface and global causal assumptions, with event-horizon formation only under additional global regularity/domain-of-outer-communications assumptions; replace compactness >1 by a sufficient quantitative trapped-surface/ANEC-deficit condition; state the bounded ANEC relaxation as an integrated focusing bound rather than an unspecified relaxation.
alternative_explanations: Collapse could fail to form a closed trapped surface due to pressure, rotation, or nonspherical dynamics despite high compactness.
Future null-geodesic incompleteness may correspond to a naked singularity rather than an event-horizon-bounded black-hole region.
A bounded ANEC relaxation may still admit stress-energy configurations that prevent focusing or horizon formation.
Observational signatures of black holes are indirect inferences of horizon-like geometry, not direct observation of trapped surfaces.
debate_trace.final_scope: Classical GR theorem: a quantitative trapped-surface condition plus global causal assumptions entails future null-geodesic incompleteness and a nonempty black-hole region; event-horizon formation and astrophysical existence require additional assumptions and are not empirically established.

debate_trace.target_claim: The candidate's central claim is that, in classical general relativity, a globally hyperbolic asymptotically flat spacetime with a noncompact Cauchy surface, a closed future outer trapped surface lying in the domain of outer communications, and a bounded integrated ANEC-deficit focusing condition entails future null-geodesic incompleteness and a nonempty black-hole region.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The claim must separate a sufficient trapped-surface theorem from necessity and observational uniqueness; the trapped-surface-in-domain-of-outer-communications assumption is imprecise and potentially conflicts with black-hole-region interpretation.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: Horizonless ultracompact objects, nontrapped collapse, naked-singularity scenarios, or quantum backreaction could explain compact-object observations or incompleteness without satisfying the proposed trapped-surface condition.
debate_trace.required_revision: Remove the assumption that the trapped surface lies in the domain of outer communications; state that the trapped-surface condition is sufficient rather than necessary; and add explicit alternative-explanation boundaries for horizonless ultracompact objects and nontrapped collapse.
alternative_explanations: Horizonless ultracompact objects or exotic matter configurations could mimic black-hole observational signatures without a closed trapped surface.
Nontrapped collapse, cosmological horizons, or naked-singularity scenarios could produce incompleteness or compactness without a classical black-hole region.
Quantum backreaction or violations of the bounded null-convergence/ANEC-deficit condition could prevent the Raychaudhuri focusing argument.
debate_trace.final_scope: A qualified classical GR theorem: a closed future outer trapped surface satisfying a quantitative null-convergence-deficit focusing bound in a globally hyperbolic asymptotically flat spacetime is sufficient for null-geodesic incompleteness and, when the trapped-surface/focusing argument excludes the surface from future null infinity, for a nonempty black-hole region; it is not necessary, not an observational proof, not a claim that all supermassive stars form black holes, and not a regular event-horizon claim without extra assumptions.

debate_trace.target_claim: If a burnout supermassive-star spacetime contains a closed two-surface satisfying the unified trapped-surface condition with compactness above C_*(E_max), then the outgoing null congruence focuses, a trapped surface forms, and Penrose-style causal geodesic incompleteness follows; if the condition or bound is violated, a counterexample boundary prevents the conclusion.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate conflates Penrose-style geodesic incompleteness with black-hole existence, uses only negative outgoing null expansion where a closed future-trapped surface normally requires both future null expansions to be negative, and misstates the relaxed integrated energy condition as a necessary ablation rather than a sufficient relaxation.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: Even with a trapped surface and an integrated focusing bound, the theorem may not imply an event horizon without cosmic censorship or asymptotic predictability, and integrated energy bounds may fail to guarantee Raychaudhuri focusing if shear, pressure gradients, or tidal terms dominate.
debate_trace.required_revision: Reduce the claim from black-hole existence to a formal trapped-surface/geodesic-incompleteness theorem; require both future null expansions for a closed trapped surface; remove ablation/necessity language; state the integrated null-energy bound as sufficient, not necessary; add cosmic-censorship or horizon-interpretation conditions if black-hole language is retained.
alternative_explanations: Astrophysical black-hole existence may require event-horizon evidence or a cosmic-censorship assumption, not only trapped-surface formation and geodesic incompleteness.
A pointwise null-energy condition or a stronger integrated curvature bound may be required if shear and tidal terms prevent persistent focusing.
Non-spherical collapse with pressure gradients may form horizons or singularities without satisfying the proposed quasi-local compactness criterion.
debate_trace.final_scope: A formal general-relativistic theorem: under global hyperbolicity, bounded shear/curvature, negligible post-burnout pressure, and an integrated null-energy focusing bound, a closed future-trapped two-surface with both null expansions negative can be constructed when quasi-local compactness exceeds a derived bound, implying Penrose-style causal geodesic incompleteness; event-horizon or black-hole interpretation is conditional on cosmic censorship or asymptotic predictability and is not direct observational proof.

debate_trace.target_claim: A relaxed integrated null-energy trapped-surface theorem provides a sufficient formal mechanism for Penrose-style causal geodesic incompleteness in globally hyperbolic burnout supermassive-star collapse spacetimes, with event-horizon or black-hole interpretation only conditional.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate must avoid overclaiming that the proposed trapped-surface theorem uniquely explains black-hole existence; it should state sufficiency, non-uniqueness, and the conditional horizon interpretation.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: A competing mechanism or confounder could explain the same formal observation: other energy-condition singularity theorems, pressure, rotation, shear, magnetic fields, quantum negative energy, bounces, or failure of cosmic censorship could produce or block the same conclusion.
debate_trace.required_revision: Add explicit alternative-explanation and scope boundaries: state that the theorem is a sufficient, non-unique formal route to geodesic incompleteness; identify competing formal mechanisms and confounders; and retain black-hole or event-horizon language only under cosmic-censorship or horizon-formation assumptions.
alternative_explanations: Other singularity theorems using pointwise null-energy conditions or different quasi-local mass definitions can imply the same geodesic incompleteness without the proposed integrated bound.
Pressure, rotation, magnetic fields, shear, or tidal terms may prevent trapped-surface formation or produce bounce-like or non-black-hole collapse histories.
Quantum or semi-classical negative energy can violate integrated focusing bounds and yield alternative collapse or singularity mechanisms.
Geodesic incompleteness may occur without an event horizon if cosmic censorship or asymptotic predictability fails, so black-hole existence is not uniquely inferred.
Non-asymptotically flat or non-globally hyperbolic spacetimes can produce incompleteness or horizon-like structures under different global assumptions.
debate_trace.final_scope: A sufficient formal theorem for Penrose-style geodesic incompleteness under trapped-surface, energy, and global-hyperbolicity assumptions; not an unconditional proof of astrophysical black-hole existence, not direct observational evidence, and not a claim that alternative singularity mechanisms are absent.

debate_trace.target_claim: In a smooth, time-orientable, asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic stellar-collapse spacetime, if a closed trapped surface exists and the averaged null-convergence deficit delta is below the Raychaudhuri focusing bound delta_focus(C), then future null geodesic incompleteness follows; within collapse_validity_domain this constitutes black-hole formation. If delta>=delta_focus(C) or no closed trapped surface forms, the entailment fails.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The central relation overidentifies black-hole formation with future null geodesic incompleteness. Penrose-type trapped-surface arguments prove singularity or geodesic incompleteness under energy and causal assumptions; they do not by themselves establish an event horizon or that the incompleteness is hidden inside a black hole. The averaged null-convergence deficit also needs an explicit affine-length average and a focusing bound tied to the initial trapped-surface expansion, not merely compactness C.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: An alternative formal explanation is that a relaxed averaged deficit can still fail to focus null generators if negative-energy bursts are concentrated outside the averaging window, if twist or caustic structure is not controlled, or if a singularity is naked rather than enclosed by an event horizon.
debate_trace.required_revision: Reduce the primary target_relation to future null geodesic incompleteness under a precisely defined averaged null-convergence deficit and Raychaudhuri focusing bound; make black-hole formation conditional on an explicit event-horizon/no-naked-singularity validity condition, and state that proof-level verification does not satisfy direct_observation.
alternative_explanations: future null geodesic incompleteness can occur without a black-hole event horizon if the singularity is naked or the causal boundary is not asymptotically flat
a bounded averaged null-convergence deficit may be insufficient if negative energy is concentrated in short bursts outside the relevant focusing interval
ordinary stellar collapse may fail to form a closed trapped surface because pressure, rotation, magnetic stresses, or quantum effects prevent inward convergence
debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified formal theorem: in smooth, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat stellar-collapse spacetimes with a closed trapped surface and a precisely bounded averaged null-convergence deficit below the Raychaudhuri focusing bound, future null geodesic incompleteness follows; black-hole formation is inferred only when the collapse_validity_domain additionally includes an event-horizon/no-naked-singularity condition. No direct empirical observation is claimed.

debate_trace.target_claim: In ordinary asymptotically flat globally hyperbolic stellar collapse, a closed trapped surface plus a bounded averaged null-convergence deficit below a Raychaudhuri focusing bound entails future null geodesic incompleteness; black-hole formation follows only if the incompleteness is enclosed by an event horizon or naked-singularity causal pathologies are excluded.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The theorem's marginal contribution must be separated from the standard Penrose trapped-surface theorem and from nontrapped or horizonless singularity mechanisms; otherwise the same geodesic incompleteness could be explained by stronger pointwise energy axioms, other singularity theorems, or an assumed horizon condition.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: A competing mechanism could explain the same formal observation: the standard pointwise null-convergence Penrose theorem when delta=0, other Hawking-Penrose or timelike-convergence singularity results, nontrapped singularities, or realistic rotating, magnetized, or quantum collapse mechanisms that form horizons without satisfying the relaxed averaged-deficit premises.
debate_trace.required_revision: State explicitly that the nonstandard claim is limited to 0<delta<delta_focus(C), that delta=0 is recovered by the standard Penrose theorem, and that black-hole existence is not inferred unless an event-horizon/no-naked-singularity condition is independently established; add proof-level boundaries for nontrapped and horizonless alternatives.
alternative_explanations: Standard Penrose theorem with pointwise null-convergence or energy conditions explains future null geodesic incompleteness when delta=0.
Other singularity theorems or nontrapped causal/geodesic pathologies can produce incompleteness without closed trapped surfaces.
Horizonless naked singularities or non-global-hyperbolic spacetimes can produce incompleteness without black-hole formation.
Realistic rotating, magnetized, or quantum collapse may satisfy black-hole formation through different energy or global-structure mechanisms than the relaxed averaged-deficit theorem.
debate_trace.final_scope: A qualified formal sufficient condition for future null geodesic incompleteness in smooth globally hyperbolic asymptotically flat ordinary GR stellar collapse, including idealized supermassive stellar collapse when the premises hold. The black-hole existence reading is conditional on an event-horizon/no-naked-singularity validity domain and does not close the direct-observation gap.

debate_trace.target_claim: The candidate claims that observable stellar-collapse proxies plus a relaxed null-energy condition imply a closed trapped surface and Penrose-style geodesic incompleteness, thereby providing a formal route to black-hole existence.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The candidate conflates a Penrose trapped-surface/singularity theorem with black-hole existence and treats stellar-collapse observables as sufficient for a closed trapped surface without specifying a quasi-local geometric criterion. It also needs to separate the observable-to-trapped-surface implication from the trapped-surface-to-incompleteness implication, and it must state the extra assumptions needed for an event-horizon/black-hole-region conclusion.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: Nonsingular compact-object, bounce, or quantum-gravity models may satisfy compactness and luminosity-decay proxies without forming trapped surfaces, and an averaged/finite-flux energy condition may be too weak to guarantee the Penrose conjugate-point step unless it is specified as a sufficient integral focusing condition.
debate_trace.required_revision: Reframe the claim as a conditional Penrose-style theorem: define observable_trapped_surface_criterion as a quasi-local observable-to-negative-null-expansion relation, derive trapped_surface_condition from that criterion, derive geodesic_incompleteness_relation under an integral/finite-flux null convergence condition sufficient for Raychaudhuri focusing, and add event-horizon/black-hole-region assumptions only if future null infinity and causal isolation are imposed. Replace the non-scientific falsifier with a formal countermodel or proof failure.
alternative_explanations: A horizonless ultracompact object or nonsingular stellar remnant could produce compactness and luminosity-decay proxies without a closed trapped surface.
A quantum bounce or sustained negative null flux could satisfy bounded-energy proxies while preventing the Penrose conjugate-point step.
Geodesic incompleteness may occur without a globally defined event horizon if future null infinity is absent or asymptotic predictability fails.
The direct_observation evidence deficit may remain empirical even if a formal observable-to-geometry relation is constructed.
debate_trace.final_scope: Conditional Penrose-style trapped-surface/singularity theorem for classical, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat massive or supermassive stellar collapse, with a qualified event-horizon/black-hole-region conclusion only under additional future-null-infinity and causal-isolation assumptions; it does not assert direct empirical detection or universal black-hole existence.

debate_trace.target_claim: If a collapsing stellar remnant contains a regular closed two-sphere satisfying a quasi-local observable trapped-surface criterion, especially negative future outgoing and ingoing null expansions, then under classical Einstein equations, global hyperbolicity, asymptotic flatness, and an integral/finite-flux null convergence condition the sphere is a closed trapped surface and the spacetime is null geodesically incomplete; with future null infinity and causal isolation, the trapped surface lies behind an event horizon.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The substituted observable trapped-surface criterion must not be conflated with empirical direct observation. In particular, stellar-collapse proxies such as compactness or luminosity decay may be gauge- and model-dependent and may not by themselves entail negative null expansions on a closed two-sphere.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: A competing mechanism or confounder could explain the same proxy signature: stable horizonless ultracompact objects, quantum or classical bounces, anisotropic stresses, sustained negative null flux, or coordinate/gauge artifacts might produce high compactness or luminosity-decay signals without forming a closed trapped surface or an event horizon.
debate_trace.required_revision: Reduce the claim to a conditional formal theorem in which negative null expansions are the operative trapped-surface premise; treat R < 2M and stellar-collapse proxies as sufficient only when explicitly derivable under stated symmetry and gauge assumptions; add horizonless compact objects, bounces, and proxy inference failures as counterexample boundaries; separate trapped-surface/geodesic-incompleteness claims from event-horizon claims.

debate_trace.required_revision: Reduce the claim to a formal sufficient condition for marginally trapped tube or apparent-horizon formation under quasi-spherical general relativity and positive/null energy conditions, and add global no-bounce and asymptotic-flatness conditions before inferring black_hole_existence_relation; explicitly state that the result bounds rather than resolves the direct_observation deficit.

debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified formal theorem for quasi-spherical general-relativistic stellar collapse: a finite-time Misner-Sharp compactness crossing, defined by vanishing outgoing null expansion, is a sufficient dynamical construction of a marginally trapped tube/apparent horizon; black-hole/event-horizon existence follows only with continued collapse, positive/null energy, asymptotic flatness, global causality, and no bounce. debate_trace.target_claim: Under classical, spherically symmetric or quasi-spherical GR, if nuclear burnout reduces pressure support enough that a closed two-surface in a collapsing supermassive core satisfies 2M_MS/R > 1, then both future-directed null expansions are negative and a closed trapped surface forms. Rotation, magnetic fields, pressure anisotropy, or non-spherical collapse can alter apparent-horizon formation and the relation between Misner-Sharp compactness and trapped surfaces.
Quantum degeneracy pressure, neutron-star support, bounce effects, or modified-gravity pressure corrections can prevent horizon formation even when classical stellar collapse is expected.
Radiation losses, neutrino transport, or equation-of-state uncertainties may change the pressure-support condition that triggers collapse.
Primordial collapse, direct-collapse pathways, mergers, or other non-stellar mechanisms can produce black holes without supermassive stellar burnout.
debate_trace.final_scope: A conditional formal theorem for classical, asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic, spherically symmetric or quasi-spherical massive or supermassive stellar cores: burnout-induced pressure-support failure is a sufficient mechanism for trapped-surface formation when Misner-Sharp compactness exceeds unity, and black-hole-region existence follows only with an explicit non-escape/horizon condition. The claim is not a universal explanation of all black holes and not observational confirmation.

debate_trace.target_claim: If a globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat classical spacetime satisfying Einstein equations contains a compact smooth spacelike two-surface S with negative future null expansions and T_ab k^a k^b >= 0 for all null k in J^+(S), then S lies in B = M - J^-(I^+) and future causal geodesics are incomplete.

debate_trace.required_revision: Narrow the theorem to future null geodesic incompleteness and nonempty black-hole region under global hyperbolicity, asymptotic flatness, and future asymptotic predictability; replace 'future causal geodesics' with 'future-directed null geodesic incompleteness' and avoid asserting S lies in B unless that is derived as part of the proof.
alternative_explanations: Informal stellar burnout and collapse can be a heuristic description rather than a formal proof.
Apparent-horizon or marginally outer trapped surface formation may provide an alternative local diagnostic for trapped-surface construction.
NEC-violating matter, non-globally hyperbolic spacetimes, or quantum-gravity effects could block the classical trapped-surface conclusion.
debate_trace.final_scope: Formal classical-GR theorem: in a globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat, future-asymptotically predictable spacetime satisfying the null-energy condition on J^+(S), a closed future-trapped surface S implies a nonempty black-hole region and future null geodesic incompleteness; it does not assert that all future causal geodesics are incomplete or that observed supermassive black holes are directly proven.

Other classical trapped-surface routes, such as nonspherical collapse, high-energy collisions, or accretion-induced collapse, can yield black holes without satisfying the proposed integrated focusing-compactness crossing.
Selection, calibration, or model bias in gravitational-wave population inference can mimic or obscure formation-channel signatures.
Beyond-GR compact objects or non-classical formation channels can mimic black-hole observables and lie outside the theorem's validity domain.

debate_trace.target_claim: By replacing classical pointwise energy conditions with averaged null energy conditions (AANEC), a formal theorem can be constructed that bounds the maximum mass of a non-black-hole compact remnant, formally deriving the observational lower mass gap (2-5 solar masses) as a consequence of horizon formation necessity.

Under these assumptions, a compactness threshold may imply trapped-surface formation and bound stable non-black-hole remnants within the stated model class. It does not quantitatively derive the observed 2-5 solar mass gap, nor does it establish black-hole existence for all realistic stellar collapse, where explosion physics, equation of state, rotation, magnetic fields, fallback, and binary evolution may dominate.

debate_trace.opponent_concern: The result may be read as explaining why black holes exist in nature, but the formal mechanism only supplies a sufficient trapped-surface construction; black-hole existence can also be certified by other closed trapped surfaces or global causal assumptions, and the ablation shows failure of this construction, not necessity of the compactness condition.
debate_trace.required_revision: Tighten the theorem to spherical or quasi-local near-spherical settings with controlled shear, distinguish C>=1 as marginally outer trapped from C>1 or C>=1 plus strict focusing as closed trapped, and reduce the claim to a qualified formal sufficient condition rather than direct observational black-hole existence.
alternative_explanations: Penrose-type black-hole existence follows from any closed trapped surface plus global hyperbolicity and an appropriate energy condition, not necessarily from this specific energy-compactness invariant.

In exact spherical symmetry, Misner-Sharp compactness directly characterizes apparent and trapped surfaces; in nonspherical collapse, hoop-conjecture-like quasi-local mass bounds or numerical GR constructions may be needed.

debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified formal sufficient theorem for classical spherical or near-spherical stellar remnants in asymptotically flat general relativity with global hyperbolicity; it proves black-hole existence only conditional on closed trapped-surface formation and does not claim direct observational proof.

debate_trace.target_claim: Under classical spherical or near-spherical collapse in asymptotically flat spacetime with global hyperbolicity outside the forming horizon, a well-defined quasi-local compactness C>1 on a closed 2-surface, together with ANEC along null generators, is sufficient to make outgoing null expansion negative and construct a closed trapped surface, hence a black hole; C>=1 alone yields only a marginally outer trapped surface unless strict focusing is added, and removing the compactness/focusing assumption invalidates this construction.

debate_trace.opponent_concern: A pre-existing trapped surface, shell crossing, coordinate-dependent compactness, uncontrolled shear, or quantum/exotic stress-energy could explain the same formal outcome without demonstrating black-hole formation from stellar burnout.
debate_trace.required_revision: Replace ANEC with local null convergence or a proved averaged-focusing lemma; make C>1 an invariant Misner-Sharp trapped-surface criterion with regularity and pre-existing-horizon exclusions; reduce the claim to a conditional formal trapped-surface/Penrose theorem.

Shell crossing or singular mass shells could produce apparent compactness without regular stellar remnant collapse.
Coordinate-dependent mass or radius definitions could fake C>1.
Uncontrolled shear or nonspherical dynamics could prevent trapped-surface formation.
Quantum backreaction or exotic stress-energy could violate local null convergence.
debate_trace.final_scope: Qualified formal sufficient theorem for classical spherical or near-spherical collapse in asymptotically flat GR: invariant C>1 plus local null convergence or a proved averaged-focusing lemma, controlled shear, and regularity constructs a closed trapped surface and supports a Penrose-type black-hole existence result; C=1 is marginal unless strict focusing is separately proved. It does not provide direct observational proof, prove supermassive burnout necessity, establish event-horizon observability, or cover generic nonspherical collapse.

debate_trace.target_claim: Within classical general relativity, a closed trapped surface together with a relaxed integrated null-convergence/compactness condition suffices to derive black-hole existence as future causal geodesic incompleteness, and removing the integrated bound yields a formal counterexample.
debate_trace.scientific_concern: The stated integrated null-convergence bound and compactness assumption are not yet a well-formed relaxation of the null energy condition: the sign/threshold is under-specified and may be too strong or false, C=2GM/(Rc^2)>=1 is not a general theorem assumption and is redundant where a trapped surface already encodes the relevant mass-radius relation, and future causal geodesic incompleteness is a singularity relation rather than a full event-horizon black-hole claim unless asymptotic predictability and horizon arguments are explicit.
debate_trace.opponent_concern: Penrose's theorem already gives black-hole-forming incompleteness under pointwise null energy plus trapped surface and global predictability; a relaxed condition may be unnecessary, equivalent to the standard condition, or invalid, while realistic stellar burnout may fail to produce a trapped surface or may be altered by quantum/exotic bounce effects.
debate_trace.required_revision: Recalibrate the claim as a conditional formal theorem: replace the fixed integrated bound/compactness assumption with a proof-validated relaxed null-convergence condition (a comparison/integral control of the negative part of R_ab k^a k^b sufficient for Raychaudhuri focusing), demote compactness to a spherical stellar diagnostic, and define black_hole_existence_relation as black-hole-forming future causal geodesic incompleteness under asymptotic predictability, not direct observational black-hole existence.

Trapped surfaces may arise from non-stellar collapse or numerical initial data, so stellar burnout is not the only mechanism.
Future causal geodesic incompleteness may indicate a singularity without, by itself, proving a globally defined event horizon unless asymptotic predictability is used.
Quantum stress-energy, bounce scenarios, or exotic matter could avoid classical incompleteness while still producing compact objects.
A compactness diagnostic may correlate with collapse but is not the causal mechanism for the theorem.
debate_trace.final_scope: Conditional classical GR theorem for asymptotically predictable stellar-collapse remnants that admit a genuine trapped surface and satisfy a proof-validated relaxed null-convergence condition; it yields black-hole-forming future causal geodesic incompleteness, with event-horizon language only under the stated predictability assumptions.

It does not claim to explain all black holes, prove stellar burnout formation from first principles, or establish observational black-hole existence.

Trapped-surface formation can be derived from stronger global energy conditions or from large incoming energy flux/initial-data criteria in non-spherical collapse.
Semiclassical negative energy or quantum stress-energy can violate averaged null-convergence conditions, changing horizon formation.
The direct_observation gap may require empirical horizon signatures, which a formal theta_l < 0 observable does not satisfy.
debate_trace.final_scope: Classical, spherically symmetric (Misner-Sharp) smooth asymptotically flat stellar-shell collapse; formal trapped-surface formation and event-horizon existence under global hyperbolicity and future null infinity; not generic non-spherical collapse, quantum gravity, or direct astronomical verification.

stable compact remnant below black-hole formation
horizonless mimicker reproducing compactness or ringdown constraints
local NEC violation with insufficient averaged Raychaudhuri focusing
quantum-gravity or modified-Raychaudhuri effects invalidating classical focusing

debate_trace.final_scope: Classical GR massive or supermassive post-burnout stellar cores that are smooth, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat, pressure-insufficient, and contain a closed future-trapped surface satisfying an explicit sufficient integrated Raychaudhuri focusing bound. Verification reversal uses existing horizon-consistent compactness and ringdown signatures only to exclude a specified regular bounce, stable-remnant, or horizonless-mimicker class when that class violates the horizon-consistent predicates; it does not prove collapse from observations or exclude all alternatives.

Future null geodesic incompleteness may occur without a globally hidden black-hole region if asymptotic flatness or cosmic-censorship assumptions fail.

Black holes formed by mergers, accretion-induced collapse, or direct dynamical collapse rather than supermassive stellar exhaustion.
Horizonless compact objects, gravastars, or quantum-bounce remnants that mimic black-hole signatures without a trapped-surface-to-event-horizon inference.
Failure of cosmic censorship or absence of a well-defined future null infinity, allowing trapped surfaces without a nonempty black-hole region.
Rotation, magnetic fields, radiation pressure, or quantum pressure preventing trapped-surface formation in stellar collapse.

An event-horizon black-hole remnant follows only with an additional horizon-forming or weak-cosmic-censorship boundary condition. The result does not prove stellar burnout, supermassiveness, empirical black-hole existence, or exclusion of alternatives.

Null geodesic incompleteness may signal a naked singularity unless future asymptotic predictability or cosmic censorship is assumed.
NEC violation or quantum effects can evade the Penrose theorem without necessarily eliminating horizon formation.

legacy_best_entry.title: A Qualified AANEC Trapped-Surface Bound for Non-Black-Hole Stellar Remnants
legacy_best_entry.abstract: This idea refines the proposed AANEC-based theorem that a bound on the maximum mass of a non-black-hole compact remnant could be derived and that the observed 2-5 solar-mass gap would follow from horizon-formation necessity. The limitation being repaired is that averaged null energy conditions are weaker than the pointwise null/strong energy conditions used in Penrose-type trapped-surface arguments, and the observed stellar mass gap is strongly affected by supernova explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, and binary evolution. We therefore construct a qualified formal theorem or conjecture: in classical general relativity under spherical symmetry, global hyperbolicity, regular matter fields, complete null generators, AANEC, and an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, a compactness threshold forces trapped-surface formation and bounds the maximum mass of stable horizonless compact remnants within the stated model class. The 2-5 solar-mass gap is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint, not a direct numerical consequence of the theorem.
legacy_best_entry.core_contribution: A formal condition-relaxation result: AANEC plus an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing assumption and stellar-structure assumptions yields a trapped-surface/compactness bound that limits the maximum mass of non-black-hole compact remnants in a restricted classical GR model, while explicitly separating the theorem from the astrophysical origin of the observed stellar lower mass gap.
legacy_best_entry.method: The method repairs the original AANEC mass-gap proposal by replacing an unqualified derivation of the 2-5 solar-mass gap with a bounded theorem/conjecture. Starting from Penrose-type trapped-surface arguments, it substitutes pointwise NEC/SEC assumptions with AANEC along complete null generators, then adds an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition sufficient for Raychaudhuri-type focusing. Using spherical collapse geometry and Misner-Sharp compactness, it derives a threshold compactness or mass scale above which a stable horizonless remnant cannot avoid trapped-surface formation within the model class. TOV-like stellar-structure assumptions are used to translate the compactness threshold into an upper mass bound for non-black-hole remnants. Boundary tests include AANEC violation, failure of averaged focusing, incomplete null generators, quantum stress-energy corrections, rotation, anisotropy, and nonspherical collapse. The observed 2-5 solar-mass gap is then compared only as an astrophysical consistency check, not as a theorem-derived prediction.
legacy_best_entry.risks: The main risks are that AANEC may be too weak to imply the needed focusing unless the added averaged null-convergence/focusing condition is strong, potentially limiting the claimed relaxation; the derived bound may apply only to restricted spherical, nonrotating, isotropic-pressure models and may not exclude exotic horizonless compact objects; and the observed 2-5 solar-mass gap may be dominated by supernova engine physics, fallback, equation-of-state uncertainties, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, binary evolution, or pair-instability processes rather than by a pure general-relativistic mass bound.
